Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (impression integrating transcript and DDx): Suspected acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina / NSTEMI) given central chest pressure with exertional onset, left arm symptoms, dyspnea, and significant cardiovascular risk factors.
- Key differential diagnoses that support or refine the impression:
  - Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina / NSTEMI) — High likelihood: central chest pressure with left arm radiation, dyspnea, nausea, significant risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidemia, smoking).
  - Pulmonary embolism — Medium likelihood: acute chest symptoms with dyspnea and leg symptoms (calf pain/swelling) suggesting possible DVT/PE.
  - Musculoskeletal chest wall pain (costochondral strain) — Medium likelihood: onset during gardening and chest wall location/pressure quality.
  - Pericarditis/myocarditis — Low likelihood: possible inflammatory cardiac etiology but less favored given risk factors and presentation.
- Conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.
- Plan:
  - Ambulance transport to hospital for urgent cardiac and respiratory evaluation.
  - Parametric monitoring en route; communicate clinical information to receiving team.
  - Avoid taking any additional medications until evaluated by emergency services/hospital.
  - Consultant at hospital to assess, with rapid access to evaluation and management; clinician will be contacted after transfer.
